Two-role annotation procedure: selectors rank words by informativeness for predicting final word, predictors attempt to guess final word using revealed words
Rationale defined as words revealed before correct prediction
Annotators (selectors) rank words by how informative they are for predicting the final word; predictors then try to predict the final word using the selected words.

Selectors rank words by how informative they are for predicting the final word; predictors attempt to guess the final word after seeing one word at a time in the order chosen by the selector. The rationale is formed by the words revealed before the predictor correctly guesses the target word or a synonym.
